sections.title: Judge the outside, not the weight matrices
paragraphs: Inside lessons taught how scores, steps and vectors work. Outside evaluation asks a different question: given this {{prompt}} and these answers, which behavior is acceptable?
Acme wants a support bot grounded in policy docs. Your outside job is to freeze the task, freeze failure modes and score answers with a {{rubric}}.
A {{goldenSet}} is the deck of reusable {{testCase}}s you will rerun. Start from refunds, EU returns, angry tone, plan price, shipping and uncovered damage.
Vague instructions like "help the customer" invite invention. Constrained instructions name format, refusal rules and the ban on invented prices.
This lesson is dedicated outside practice. You are not training {{weights}} here. You are building evidence for a later harness run in AiEval.

check.prompt: A PM says the new model "feels nicer" in Slack. What outside artifact is still missing?
check.answer: A golden set and rubric with scored evidence
choices: A golden set and rubric with scored evidence
check.explanation: Feelings are not an evaluation. Outside craft needs fixed {{testCase}}s and anchored {{criterion}} rows so you can defend a decision.

sections.title: Build the deck and the anchors
paragraphs: Write at least these failure tags into your deck: wrong refund window, missing EU policy, angry tone, price hallucination, shipping SLA and over-claim on coverage.
Use three {{criterion}} rows: Accuracy, Tone and Faithfulness. Anchor 1 / 3 / 5 so two reviewers can argue with the same language.
Compare two canned replies to the plan-price question. The strong reply cites $9 from policy. The weak reply invents $15 and an unlimited refund.
Click each reveal. Score the weak reply low on Accuracy and Faithfulness even if the tone sounds friendly.
When context is missing, a faithful answer may refuse. Do not punish honest "I do not have that information" when the docs are silent.

reveals.prompt: Strong canned reply on Plan Basic.
reveals.reveal: States $9 from policy and stays inside the docs. High Accuracy and Faithfulness.

reveals.prompt: Weak canned reply on Plan Basic.
reveals.reveal: Invented $15 and unlimited refunds. Fail Accuracy and Faithfulness even if tone is warm.

reveals.prompt: Angry refund demand with no policy match.
reveals.reveal: Stay calm, state the 14-day rule if it applies and avoid matching the customer's heat.

aside.title: Keep the Acme deck
aside.body: You will paste these {{testCase}}s into AiEval in the next labs. Keep Accuracy, Tone and Faithfulness as your starter {{rubric}}.

check.prompt: Which canned Plan Basic answer should win on Faithfulness?
check.answer: The reply that states $9 from policy without extras
choices: The reply that states $9 from policy without extras
The reply that invents $15 and unlimited refunds
Any reply that uses exclamation marks
A reply that ignores the question entirely
check.explanation: Faithfulness rewards claims supported by context. Invented prices fail even when the tone is cheerful.

sections.title: Hand the deck to the harness
paragraphs: You now have an outside artifact: constrained Acme instructions, six {{testCase}} ideas and a three-row {{rubric}}.
Branch spur on the Learn hub: First evaluation lab warms up AiEval's generate → score → compare loop. Support bot decision lab asks for a ship / ship-other / neither call.
Those harness labs are not required for Continue. Use them when you want the live tool loop.
That is the perspective shift: models are computable inside and measurable outside. The harness is how you repeat the measurement.
Next spine step: **Regression evals**. Re-run a golden set after changes to catch quality drops.
bullets: Branch: First evaluation lab and Support bot decision lab on the hub spur.

check.prompt: In a short phrase, what should you carry into the harness labs?
check.answer: Constrained prompt, golden cases and rubric
check.explanation: The harness needs your outside artifacts. Without a fixed {{prompt}}, {{goldenSet}} and {{rubric}}, automation cannot produce a defendable decision.

recapQuestions.answer: Build evidence artifacts to judge Acme support answers
choices: Build evidence artifacts to judge Acme support answers

recapQuestions.explanation: Outside eval practice produces a {{goldenSet}} and {{rubric}} for the Acme bot so later harness runs have something real to score.

recapQuestions.prompt: A friendly answer invents a price. Which criteria should suffer first?
recapQuestions.explanation: Invented facts fail Accuracy and Faithfulness. Tone can still look fine, which is why multi-criteria {{rubric}}s matter.
